  • Vampeta è stato coinvolto in un incidente stradale nel quartiere di Vila Maria, nella zona nord di San Paolo.
  • It has been revealed that �Stavo giocando a calcio al club con i ragazzi e stavo tornando a casa.
  • Nel suo racconto, la motociclista ha riferito che stava viaggiando sotto la pioggia e aveva rallentato in prossimità di un incrocio.

Vampeta è stato coinvolto in un incidente stradale nel quartiere di Vila Maria, nella zona nord di San Paolo. In un'intervista rilasciata a SBT, l'ex Inter ha negato di aver tentato di allontanarsi dal luogo dell'incidente e ha assicurato di non aver bevuto alcolici. Inoltre, l'ex giocatore ha raccontato di aver consegnato 500 real alla donna per aiutarla a sostenere le spese per i pezzi di ricambio della moto, ma che successivamente lei avrebbe chiesto una somma maggiore.

It has been revealed that �Stavo giocando a calcio al club con i ragazzi e stavo tornando a casa. Percorrevo una strada piena di incroci. Pioveva e l'asfalto era bagnato. Sono passato con la macchina e una moto è caduta. Non sapevo nemmeno che alla guida ci fosse una ragazza. Mi sono fermato 20-30 metri più avanti e sono arrivati quattro motociclisti che fanno consegne. Uno di loro ha detto: "Questo ha i soldi". La ragazza non ha detto nulla. Quel tizio mi ha fatto perdere la pazienza. Sono tornato indietro, la ragazza era ancora lì, è arrivata una pattuglia e ho chiesto subito di fare la denuncia», ha raccontato Vampeta.

Nel suo racconto, la motociclista ha riferito che stava viaggiando sotto la pioggia e aveva rallentato in prossimità di un incrocio. In quel momento, secondo la sua versione, l'automobile guidata dall'ex calciatore sarebbe sopraggiunta ad alta velocità. Nel tentativo di frenare, avrebbe perso il controllo della moto, finendo per urtare la parte posteriore laterale della vettura. La donna, che lavora come corriere, ha inoltre dichiarato che la ruota della moto avrebbe colpito il suo casco, provocando la rottura della visiera e danneggiando anche lo specchietto retrovisore. Dopo l'impatto, Vampeta avrebbe parcheggiato alcuni metri più avanti, ma, secondo la versione della donna, avrebbe tentato di lasciare il luogo dell'incidente prima dell'arrivo della polizia. Alcuni motociclisti presenti nelle vicinanze sarebbero intervenuti, impedendogli di allontanarsi.

According to recent reports, la donna ha infine sostenuto che l'ex calciatore mostrasse un comportamento compatibile con uno stato di ebbrezza e che si sarebbe rifiutato di sottoporsi all'alcoltest. La dinamica dell'incidente e le versioni fornite dalle persone coinvolte presentano dunque delle divergenze e dovrà essere la polizia a ricostruire l'esatta dinamica.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Vincenzo Montella, ex allenatore del Milan, ha rilasciato una intervista a La Gazzetta dello Sport, ricordando i suoi tempi in rossonero.

Com'era il rapporto con Berlusconi?

It has been revealed that "A Berlusconi piaceva parlare di calcio, gli piaceva dare suggerimenti anche quando l'allenatore era un po' fuori contesto in quel momento, perché lui aveva sempre la mentalità di avere Van Basten centravanti — Pallone d'Oro — e in panchina il sostituto, Papin. Questo me lo ricordo benissimo: lui voleva che giocassimo con due punte e io cercavo di tamponare per mesi (gli attaccanti erano, Kalinie e André Silva). È difficile perché io facevo le formazioni, è difficile sbagliare formazione perché io me le ricordo tutte. Ero tifoso del Milan, quindi il titolare era Van Basten e la riserva era Papin, entrambi Palloni d'Oro. Quindi, gli dicevo, 'Se lei mi compra qualche giocatore così, stia tranquillo che li faccio giocare tutti e due'".

10 anni fa arrivava la Supercoppa a Doha.

Sources indicate that "È stato un anno in cui siamo tornati in Europa, credo fossero due o tre anni che il Milan non ci andava, ed era qualcosa di nuovo all'epoca. Abbiamo vinto un trofeo, piccolo: proprio qualche sera fa ho vistoa cena Galliani e me l'ha ricordato e lo ricordo perfettamente. Ecco, se devo dire, ho trovato un dirigente all'epoca perfetto, perché quando accompagnava qualche aneddoto su queste pressioni, stava sempre dalla mia parte, mi lasciava autonomia totale nelle scelte. Mi ha aiutato dal numero dei collaboratori a nuove cose: qualsiasi cosa chiedessi, era sempre dalla parte dell'allenatore. E quindi per me è stato un dirigente incredibile, che in quella fase lì, in quel cambio lì, è stato fondamentale anche per ottenere quei piccoli risultati, soprattutto dopo il grande Milan di Berlusconi. Noi meritavamo di vincere anche durante i tempi regolamentari: avevamo avuto alcune opportunità facili per chiuderla, poi siamo arrivati ai rigori. Gigio parò il rigore a Dybala, che calciò bello forte, ma lui la porta gliel'ha riempita".

Poi c'è stato il mercato delle cose formali...

Recent findings suggest that "Io dall'inizio era un po' preoccupato perché c'è questa mania di esternare tutto, di — insomma — quasi pubblicitario più che altro, quindi era un po' preoccupato. In teoria c'era condivisione, almeno così si palesava, ma non potevo tirarmi indietro quando in realtà non era sempre così. E quindi alcune volte c'erano dei calciatori per cui non ero neanche stato consultato, che arrivavano e che poi dicevano 'È stato condiviso': quando sei lì non puoi dire diversamente. Sicuramente, quando si costruisce una squadra e hai il budget, la prima cosa che fai è: il portiere ce l'avevamo, prendo un centravanti, ci manca il centravanti. Nella scelta di tutto era rimasto il centravanti, con un budget — se non ricordo male — sui quindici-venti milioni. E quindi poi Kalinić... lui sì, l'ho scelto io perché quello era il budget. Quindi la nostra, diciamo, seconda scelta di attaccante fu pagato trentotto milioni, se non ricordo male, che era André Silva, e il primo attaccante fu la metà. E quindi, se non ricordo male, si è creato un equivoco di questo tipo, con tanti cambi, che poi in quella fase non giocavamo neanche male per avere, credo, quindici giocatori nuovi. Avevamo ancora Calhanoglu che non stava bene, che veniva da sei mesi di inattività per squalifica, se non ricordo male: quindi, nel contesto, era in costruzione la squadra; non eravamo in linea con gli obiettivi dello scudetto che erano stati proclamati, ma sicuramente per un processo di crescita eravamo assolutamente in linea".

"All'epoca forse stavamo trattando Aubameyang, se non ricordo male".

Cristiano Ronaldo, si parlava anche di lui: ci credevi?

“No, non credevo: anzi, proprio per nulla".

Avevi contatti con la proprietà cinese?

"Siamo andati lì, erano proprietari. Col senno di poi magari diverso, però allora non erano, come dire, nocivi".

Xabi Alonso hits out at ‘soft’ Chelsea players

📅 12 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 23 min read (4640 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.
  • Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.
  • Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.

Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.

Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.

The club’s dreadful clean-sheet record pre-dates him and is the first time in 65 years Chelsea have gone 20 league games without keeping the opposition out.

It has been revealed that hull’s first goal from Mohamed Belloumi came after the ball had bounced over Jorrel Hato and Alonso said: “We need to be aware that from any situation, any team in the Premier League can hurt you. Today it was from a long ball, two bounces, the way it happened. You need to be very aware, very ready that the danger can come from any situation. If you are soft or if you are not prepared, you will get punished and we have been punished that way.”.

Chelsea have shared 30 goals with their opponents in the club’s six games in all competitions so far this season.

“Yeah, it’s all maybe entertaining, but I hope that one day you say it was a boring game and we win and we don’t give these entertaining moments,” he said.

Recent findings suggest that “But, for sure, it kind of repeats some patterns that we are making. It will take time to... or it will take moments to fix them when we get the lead and you still need to be competing and not give the chance so easily for them to come back, especially in the first goal, we can do much better.

“It was too soft to give them this hope because until then we were controlling, we were creating chances. But that momentum that we had changed the mood and the score of the game, and it’s something that we need to be talking [about], we address and we will get better. But it’s having an impact on our performances at the moment.”.

Asked if his players have a real desire to defend and keep clean sheets, Alonso mentioned: “We can do better, we can do better for sure. We need to know that even when we have the lead, a very important part of the game is to hold together, to keep the distance, to go intense in the situations to defend. I’m sure that we can do better.

“Overall, I think that we are attacking better than defending in every part. We know that it’s a massive topic and a big theme for us. For sure, it’s just four games. But the dynamic in terms of conceding, I don’t like it and we need to do much better. Open play, set-pieces, long balls, this toughness, this competitive sense, we can do better.”.

Needing three goals or more to win games is not sustainable, as Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is finding out.

Recent findings suggest that this is not a problem of Alonso’s making, given Chelsea have now gone 20 Premier League games without a clean sheet. But he is certainly not improving the issue yet.

Chelsea beat Fulham with three goals and Brighton with four but left themselves far too much to do against Arsenal and were taken advantage of by Hull City, who will be slightly disappointed they did not leave Stamford Bridge with all three points.

Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez has now conceded seven goals in three games since joining from Aston Villa, while central defender Maxence Lacroix, who joined for £52m from Crystal Palace in the summer, was relegated to the substitutes’ bench.

Martínez was at fault for Mohamed Belloumi’s second goal, but the Argentine did make a crucial save at his back post to stop substitute Mohamed-Ali Cho grabbing a winner that Chelsea could have had no complaints about.

It has been revealed that hull finished the game with more shots on goal than their hosts and a higher expected-goals rate. Chelsea are far too open and in some ways far too entertaining.

It has been revealed that defensive midfielder Moisés Caicedo cannot return from injury quickly enough, but this does not feel like a problem that will be solved by one man. Alonso needs to find a balance and instil a real desire in his team to defend.

Caicedo has that desire, but there are no defenders at the club who have shown that absolute desperation to keep the ball out of the net that Chelsea fans became so used to in the days of John Terry, Gary Cahill and César Azpilicueta.

None of this should diminish Hull’s performance. They were not only spirited and full of character but also showed quality and a threat. The joke is right now on those who laughed at their hopes of survival before a ball had been kicked.

It is now two wins and two draws for Sergej Jakirovic’s team and they are already a fifth of the way to 40 points. Jakirovic had promised his staff a week off in the international break if they reached eight points after five games. With that target already met, there may be a upcoming reward if Hull can make it 11 points against Newcastle United next weekend.

Sources indicate that “Before the season, I said to my staff that we will take seven, eight points in these first five and then I will give them seven days off,” Jakirovic said. “That was our target and now we are in a very good position, eight points.

“Especially today, it’s very, very difficult to play here, and now we will try to get even more. Of course, I’m a little bit worried about the international break because we have 13 national team players. But we will see who will come back and in what condition. So this is my concern right now.” Asked if his staff’s seven-day break will be extended if Hull can beat Newcastle, Jakirovic added: “I will tell them. But I know already.”.

It has been revealed that while his five-game target may need modifying, Jakirovic is not deviating from his goal for the season for Hull. “Our target is always to stay in the league and collect as many points as possible,” he remarked. “Forty points, 38 to 41, this is the average we need. Then it’s easier to play. You can play more relaxed, with more joy and happiness. So [get to] this as soon as possible, so that we are safe.”.

Hull had not conceded a league goal before this and there had been predictions they might crumble when they finally let the ball into their net. They did so after just seven minutes but they kept their heads and came back stronger.

It was far too easy for Morgan Rogers to make a yard of space for himself to shoot after collecting the ball from João Pedro, and Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis may not have been happy to have been beaten at his near post.

According to recent reports, chelsea have now scored inside the first 10 minutes in all of their four league games, but Hull were in no mood to crumble and hit back with two goals in six minutes from Belloumi to take a half-time lead. Both Hull goals were shockers from Chelsea’s perspective. The first, in the 28th minute, came as a result of Jorrel Hato letting the ball bounce over him from a Ryan Giles cross and Belloumi finished brilliantly.

Industry observers note that belloumi’s second came after Martínez had flapped at a corner and Semi Ajayi had hit the bar with a header. The ball fell to Belloumi again and his shot was deflected into the net.

It was no surprise that Hato did not reappear for the second half, as he was replaced by Pep Chavarría at left-back. But Chelsea remained vulnerable and Martínez had to recover from spilling a Regan Slater shot to prevent Ollie McBurnie extending Hull’s advantage.

When Palmer and Pedro combined for Pedro to sweep the ball into the net and equalise with 24 minutes remaining, it seemed like it would be Chelsea who would provide the grandstand finish.

But it was Hull who got a second wind and Chelsea were indebted to Martínez for making a save to stop Cho securing all three points and sending the visiting fans home even happier.

I feel good. We have to be happy. It’s a huge result for us.

Sources indicate that we had 2-1 at half-time and we had a 100 per cent chance with McBurnie but Martinez’s save was excellent. We have to control play better in the box because we can stop this [Chelsea goal]. We had an excellent chance for Cho – Martinez saved again. Player of the match.

In a recent development, we can be very happy. We took a point in a very demanding match.

Sources indicate that eight points against very difficult opponents. We have to continue like this.

It has been revealed that there have been 12 Premier League games at Anfield in 2026, Liverpool have only won 4 of them to date. This was seventh draw and Fulham deserves their share of the spoils. This was very much a learning experience for Andoni Iraola.

Not a single home win in the Premier League, today.

Aston Villa 1 Nottingham Forest 2Bournemouth 2 Brentford 2Chelsea 2 Hull City 2Crystal Palace 2 Ipswich Town 3Liverpool 0 Fulham 0.

What a result for Hull, who remain unbeaten and they have taken five points from fixtures against United, Villa and Chelsea.

That is the first really poor result of the Alonso era, points dropped.

What a thriller in SE25, both teams have been going for it in the closing stages, but Ipswich have surely score the winner through Zian Flemming.

Fulham were pointless before this game, but they have kept a clean sheet at Anfield with a disciplined display and they could well have score one or two. Underwhelming for Liverpool, who have not won just one of their first four games and their fixtures have not been the most taxing.

It has been revealed that and as we predicted at the beginning of the game... Liverpool 0 Fulham 0. If this reporter ever gives you advice on a horse to back or a team to follow, make sure you take the opposite stance. Fulham deserve their reward and their fans are singing “We got a point!”.

Villa are finishing the game with 10 men because Ian Maatsen pulled up after Emery had made his five substitutions, and Forest have punished them through Igor Jesus with just a few minutes of normal time to play.

Alexander Isak heads over the bar when he perhaps should have hit the target. Has time run out for Liverpool?

Recent findings suggest that you might imagine Chelsea are battering down the door, but Mohamed-Ali Cho has just forced Emi Martinez into a save at the other end. Hull will remain unbeaten if they can hold out.

Strand Larsen has had his critics, but he has scored his first goal of the season to set up a grandstand finish with 15 minutes plus stoppage time to play at Selhurst Park.

Short corner, McGinn whipped in an inswinging cross that is glanced into the bottom corner by Alysson.

It has been revealed that liverpool continue to toil at Anfield, but no opening goal. Iraola has thrown on Frimpong, Mac Allister, Ngumoha and Gakpo in the second half. Fulham have had the chances to score at least one, and Josh King has just brought a save out of Alisson.

In a recent development, hull are a little lucky they still have 11 men on the pitch. Already on a booking, my man Crooks bundled down Rogers. It could easily have been another yellow car but the referee let him off and now he’s been replaced by Iroegbunam.

Joao Pedro finds the smallest of gaps to be the goalkeeper and find the roof of the net with a brilliant, instinctive finish.

Recent findings suggest that that had not really been coming for Chelsea. It all felt a bit easy for Palmer to get his low cross into the box and Pedro to sweep the ball in. The home fans have woken up again.

Recent findings suggest that martinez was lucky to get away with another slip up, there. He spilt Slater’s shot but reacted before McBurnie to stop the Hull striker scoring the rebound. Just a day after his nasty looking crash, Sorba Thomas is on for Hull.

According to recent reports, this game is absolutely here for Fulham to win. Quietness has descended around Anfield, the hosts have no fluency in their play and Fulham are growing in confidence. Why wouldn’t they after getting to 65 minutes with a clean sheet?

Sources indicate that just like in the first half, four minutes after one of these teams taking the lead there has been an equaliser. Kevin Scahde is in a rich vein of form.

Sources indicate that bournemouth have have never beaten Brentford in the Premier League, but they might well be on their way to changing that record having trailed earlier in the game. Marcus Tavernier has just scored their second goal.

It has been revealed that matt Davidson Rider Crooks has just been booked for a very cynical foul on Rogers. It gave Chelsea a free-kick in a dangerous position Reece James had an effort tipped away. Chelsea have started the second half well.

Recent findings suggest that within a minute of the restart, Villa lose the ball in midfield and Delap punishes them to the maximum. Cracking finish from just outside the box, and a much-needed goal by Delap. The Glasner curse striking for Emery again?

Liam Delap has just started paying back that £50m transfer fee with a fine goal.

Delap picked the ball up on the left and set himself up on the edge of the box before crashing a 25-yard shot past Zion Suzuki.

Unai Emery has made a couple of changes at half-time, taking off Nicolas Jackson who picked up a silly booking just before half-time.

Tammy Abraham is on in his place. George Hemmings is also off and replaced by Alysson.

Pep Chavarria on for Chelsea at half-time. He’s replaced Jorrel Hato, who had a bit of a stinker in the first half.

Sources indicate that andoni Iraola hasn’t hung about here. Milos Kerkez has come on immediately after half-time for Kostas Tsimikas and you can say with certainty that Liverpool will be shopping for a upcoming left-back in due course.

So at half-time, Hull City are top of the Premier League and don’t their supporters know it? They were singing “we are top of the League” for the full two minutes of time added on for stoppages at the end of the first period. Alonso has some work to do at the break.

Forest did need a brilliant double save from Matz Sels to deny Victor Lindelof and have recovered to slow the match down.

Neco Williams wasted a decent chance for Forest from outside the penalty area shortly before the break.

Referee Andrew Madley has irritated both teams with a number of weird decisions - but that’s sadly par for the course with officials nowadays.

Things got worse for Palace just before half-time, with Leif Davis heading home at the back post to give Ipswich the league.

Apologies for the lack of updates, some technical gremlins at Telegraph Towers. A nip and tuck game as expected at at the Vitality: Kevin Schade gave Brentford the lead before Justin Kluivert equalised four minutes later.

One way to put it is that Kostas Tsimikas isn’t playing well. Another way to say it would be that his efforts are making Milos Kerkez look like Roberto Carlos. That’s now seven goals Emi Martinez has conceded in three games since joining from Villa to supposedly solve Chelsea’s goalkeeping crisis. Martinez won’t be pleased with Hull’s second goal, here. According to recent reports, this is a turn up for the books. Chelsea undone by a long ball forward, and Hato lets the ball bounce over his head, and Belloumi finishes with aplomb.

That’s now 20 Premier League games Chelsea have gone without keeping a clean sheet. What an earth was Jorrel Hato doing, letting the ball bounce over him for Belloumi? Amateur stuff at the back from the home side. It was Hull’s first meaningful attack.

Emersonn has struggled in some games so far this season, but he has just planted a header into the corner from a Davis cross.

Industry observers note that there is a VAR check for offside... but the goal stands.

Austin MacPhee, Chelsea’s flamboyant set-piece coach, just motioned for Xabi Alonso to sit down when the Blues manager momentarily got up from his seat when the home side were preparing to take a corner. It seems MacPhee wears the (correct length) trousers when it comes to set pieces.

An almighty let off for Alisson and Liverpool after pass from the goalkeeper played Gravenberch into trouble, but Jacquet cleared off the line to keep the game goalless. That was Fulham’s first foray forward.

According to recent reports, A bright start in this game and there is no chance it will end goalless (famous last words). Andoni Iraola has made three changes from the team that beat Atletico Madrid on Wednesday and it’s a pattern of his early management that he is making the kind of decisions that supporters are nodding along in approval with. Liverpool should already be one up but Alexander Isak’s shot has just drifted across the face of goal but the signs are encouraging. It could be a long afternoon for Alvaro Arbeloa.

It has been revealed that wow. Unbelievable double save from Forest’s Matz Sels there to keep out Victor Lindelof.

The first was the most impressive, a reflex stop after a deflection.

Morgan Rogers is the first player to score against Hull City this season. Emi Martinez launched the ball forward after claiming a corner, and Rogers’ shot from the edge of the area crept under the goalkeeper Tzolakis. He will not want to watch that one again.

We’re past five minutes and it’s the longest Chelsea have gone without scoring in the league this season. Back on Matt Crooks – one of his middle names is Rider.

Sources indicate that although Rogers scored in the seventh minute...so the early goals continue for Chelsea. It will be difficult for Hull now.

The early indications are that Reece James is playing in midfield with Malo Gusto at right-back in a conventional back four.

This is a big game and we are looking for our first three points of the season. We have been close in every game so we hope to get it today.

Unai Emery is possibly the best coach in the Premier League but has found past encounters with Oliver Glasner very uncomfortable.

Since Glasner’s arrival in English football with Crystal Palace in February 2024, he has faced Emery’s Villa seven times and never lost.

With five victories and two draws, it is an impressive record albeit with a different set of players.

Aston Villa and Forest are two teams in transition, and meet for the first time since that two-legged Europa League semi-final last season.

Villa are building a upcoming chapter after a summer of significant change, while Forest are implementing a totally different style of play under Oliver Glasner.

There have been signs of progress at both of the former European Cup winners. Villa secured an impressive victory over Club Brugge in the Champions League on Tuesday. Forest are improving under Glasner, with their best performance the 2-2 draw at Liverpool.

Returning to Villa Park will have some bitter memories for a number of the Forest players, after that 4-0 defeat in the second leg of the Europa League.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this afternoon’s Premier League three o’clock kick-offs, and home bankers would appear to be the theme of the day.

Liverpool will be strongly fancied to put Fulham to the sword at Anfield, with confidence low at the London club and latest manager Alvaro Arbeloa (once a player at Anfield) already under pressure amid reports of dressing room unrest. Andoni Iraola secured his first Premier League victory as Liverpool manager at Ipswich last time out, and backed up that result with a come-from-behind win against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

Chelsea host Hull City, who are unbeaten after three games and have yet to concede a goal. It is a remarkable start to the season for Sergej Jakirović‘s side, who continue to defy expectations as well as the underlying data. For all their spirit and defensive organisation, keeping out Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro at Stamford Bridge promises to be a tall order, though.

Aston Villa’s rocky start to the campaign took a turn for the better with a 3-2 Champions League victory at Club Brugge, and as the weeks go by Unai Emery’s team should grow stronger as their raft of young signings bed in. Nottingham Forest could be obdurate opponents, although Villa swept them aside in the second leg of last season’s Europa League semi-final. Oliver Glasner’s Crystal Palace were a bogey team for Villa though, with the Austrian coach undefeated against Emery having notched up some resounding victories.

Glasner’s former club Palace could do with a home win against Ipswich Town, while there is cigarette paper between Bournemouth and Brentford, two of the league’s smartest operators who play at the Vitality Stadium this afternoon. Bournemouth qualified for Europe at Brentford’s expense last season, but Marco Rose is looking for his first league win despite some encouraging performances.

In a recent development, il Senegal torna campione d'Africa. Il Tribunale Arbitrale dello Sport ha infatti riassegnato all'unanimità la contestata Coppa del 2025, ribaltando la decisione che aveva attribuito al Marocco il trofeo a tavolino. Il 17 marzo, la commissione d'appello della Confederazione Africana di Calcio aveva revocato il titolo al Senegal, assegnandolo al Marocco, dopo una finale segnata da incidenti ma comunque terminata.

Il Senegal a sua volta aveva presentato ricorso al Tas che, a più di dieci mesi dalla finale, ha ritenendo che l'arbitro non avesse commesso alcun errore nell'ordinare la ripresa del gioco dopo gli incidenti. Il 18 gennaio a Rabat, il Senegal aveva vinto la Coppa d'Africa battendo 1-0 il Marocco dopo i tempi supplementari e il caos, per la contestazione di un rigore assegnato al Marocco nei minuti di recupero.

La sentenza di primo grado aveva solo comminato sanzioni disciplinari, poi in appello il ko a tavolino per il Senegal, reo di aver "abbandonato il campo prima della fine prevista della partita senza il permesso dell'arbitro". La Federcalcio senegalese aveva denunciato "il più sfacciato furto nella storia del nostro sport". Ora il successo al Tas e la Coppa che torna al Senegal. Il Marocco può ancora ricorrere alla Corte federale svizzera, che non si pronuncia sul merito ma interviene sulle questioni procedurali.

'F*** the Pope and the IRA' chant lands England in hot water as fans are given suspended one-game stadium ban and FA fined

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 13:19 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 03:21 EST, 20 November 2026.
  • UEFA have slapped the FA with a £12,500 fine and a suspended one-match away supporters ban after England fans were heard singing sectarian chants during their Nations League victory over Spain last weekend.
  • Some of the 3,000 supporters who travelled to Madrid were heard singing 'f*** the Pope and the IRA' inside Madrid's Metropolitano Stadium on Sunday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 13:19 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 03:21 EST, 20 November 2026.

UEFA have slapped the FA with a £12,500 fine and a suspended one-match away supporters ban after England fans were heard singing sectarian chants during their Nations League victory over Spain last weekend.

Some of the 3,000 supporters who travelled to Madrid were heard singing 'f*** the Pope and the IRA' inside Madrid's Metropolitano Stadium on Sunday.

As a result, UEFA have fined the FA and banned away fans from attending one UEFA match for 'racist and/or discriminatory behaviour'.

That mentioned, the ban will only take effect if England supporters reoffend within the next two years.

It is a fortunate reprieve given the Three Lions' next away fixture is their Nations League quarter-final, the draw for which is on Friday.

Meanwhile, the FA have committed to identifying those involved and taking action - which could see football banning orders imposed.

In a statement to Daily Mail Sport, the FA said: 'We will not tolerate this unacceptable and deeply offensive chanting, and will work with the police who attend all England home and away matches to identify the perpetrators and take the necessary action.'.

England fans land FA in hot water over 'f*** the Pope and the IRA' chant during Spain victory.

In a recent development, england supporters have notoriously sung the anti-Catholic and loyalist chant. In 2024, the Irish police urged travelling fans to 'respect local culture' before their Nations League match against the Republic of Ireland.

Fans were also filmed in Milan city centre on the eve of the clash against Italy in 2022 singing the same incendiary chant - just one year after their European Championship final defeat to the Italians.

Meanwhile, then England boss Roy Hodgson and the FA were forced to condemn supporters after the inflammatory chant was heard throughout England's 3-1 friendly victory over Scotland at Celtic Park in 2014. Around 5,000 fans travelled to the devoutly Catholic club.

It has been revealed that the problem is not limited to international football. In August, Daily Mail Sport revealed that Chelsea wrote to supporters after a section of their fans were heard singing the sectarian chant away at Fulham on the opening weekend of the Premier League season.

England boss Thomas Tuchel was asked about racism in his pre-Spain press conference.

'I never expect racism and the dressing room is the most anti-racist place on Earth and that's exactly how it works,' Tuchel stated.

'I expect emotional and of course supporting fans from Spain for their national team. That's what I expect, but I don't expect racism nowhere.

'I'm shocked if it happens, and it should happen nowhere, and I'm the first one to stand up for these kind of values.

'My trust is that we have a friendly atmosphere, that we have an atmosphere who is clearly in favour of the Spanish team, and that football does what it does best: bring people together and not divide people.'.

Rivoluzione Coppa Italia: Inter e Inter U23 potrebbero affrontarsi in finale. Il documento

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Inter contro Inter U23 in una finale di Coppa Italia?
  • La Lega ha infatti pubblicato il bando per l’assegnazione dei diritti audiovisivi della Coppa Italia e della Supercoppa Italiana per il triennio 2027-2030, inserendo due possibili formule alternative per la coppa nazionale.
  • La novità più interessante per il mondo nerazzurro è contenuta nel cosiddetto Format B, che prevede l’allargamento della competizione a 56 squadre e apre alla partecipazione di un numero maggiore di società di Serie C, comprese potenzialmente le seconde squadre dei club di Serie A.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Inter contro Inter U23 in una finale di Coppa Italia? Uno scenario che oggi appare quasi fantascientifico, ma che trova spazio nelle ipotesi di riforma della competizione presentate dalla Lega Serie A.

La Lega ha infatti pubblicato il bando per l’assegnazione dei diritti audiovisivi della Coppa Italia e della Supercoppa Italiana per il triennio 2027-2030, inserendo due possibili formule alternative per la coppa nazionale.

La novità più interessante per il mondo nerazzurro è contenuta nel cosiddetto Format B, che prevede l’allargamento della competizione a 56 squadre e apre alla partecipazione di un numero maggiore di società di Serie C, comprese potenzialmente le seconde squadre dei club di Serie A.

Ma c’è un passaggio particolarmente curioso.

�Le Seconde Squadre non possono incontrare le rispettive Prime Squadre se non in Finale».

Questo significa che, qualora venisse adottata la nuova formula e l’Inter U23 ottenesse il diritto di partecipare, la formazione di Cristian Chivu e la seconda squadra nerazzurra non potrebbero affrontarsi nei turni precedenti alla finale.

Un eventuale incrocio tra le due formazioni sarebbe dunque consentito soltanto nell’atto conclusivo della competizione.

Naturalmente si tratta di una possibilità puramente teorica, che richiederebbe a entrambe le squadre di raggiungere la finale.

Per l’Inter U23, tuttavia, sarebbe un’opportunità importante per confrontarsi anche con avversarie delle categorie superiori.

Sources indicate that MONZA, ITALY - FEBRUARY 04: General view inside the dressing room ahead of Coppa Italia match between FC Internazionale and Torino FC at U-Power Stadium on February 04, 2026 in Monza, Italy. (Photo by Mattia Pistoia - Inter/Inter via Getty Images).

Il Format A ripropone sostanzialmente l’attuale struttura della Coppa Italia.

Il Format B, invece, introduce una serie di modifiche significative:.

•⁠ ⁠56 squadre partecipanti: 20 di Serie A, 20 di Serie B e 16 di Serie C. •⁠ ⁠Ingresso delle otto teste di serie ai sedicesimi, anziché agli ottavi di finale. •⁠ ⁠Semifinali in gara unica, eliminando il doppio confronto di andata e ritorno. •⁠ ⁠Possibilità per le seconde squadre di partecipare in base ai criteri previsti. •⁠ ⁠Impossibilità per le seconde squadre di affrontare le rispettive prime squadre prima della finale.

Per le grandi società di Serie A, dunque, cambierebbe anche il percorso verso la conquista del trofeo.

Le otto teste di serie dovrebbero iniziare la competizione un turno prima rispetto a oggi, ma l’eliminazione delle semifinali di andata e ritorno compenserebbe l’impegno supplementare.

Inizialmente, il Format B prevedeva una corsia preferenziale per le seconde squadre delle società di Serie A, indipendentemente dal campionato nel quale militassero.

Secondo quanto riportato da Tuttomercatoweb nella serata del 24 novembre, la Lega Serie A ha successivamente corretto il testo, eliminando questa priorità.

Si sarebbe trattato di un errore materiale nella stesura del documento.

In caso di adozione del nuovo formato, dunque, le sedici società provenienti dalla Serie C verrebbero individuate secondo criteri di merito, senza favorire automaticamente le seconde squadre.

Anche l’Inter U23, quindi, dovrebbe conquistare sul campo il diritto di partecipare alla competizione, secondo i criteri che saranno stabiliti.

La Lega ha infatti presentato entrambe le ipotesi agli operatori televisivi interessati all’acquisto dei diritti per le stagioni 2027/28, 2028/29 e 2029/30.

Le offerte economiche delle emittenti contribuiranno a determinare quale delle due formule verrà adottata.

Il Format B, che comprende più partite e una partecipazione più ampia delle società di Serie C, potrebbe quindi entrare in vigore a partire dalla stagione 2027/28.

E per l’Inter si aprirebbe anche uno scenario davvero particolare: vedere la propria seconda squadra partecipare alla stessa Coppa Italia della prima formazione, con la possibilità di un derby nerazzurro soltanto in finale.

Una prospettiva ancora lontana, ma che per la prima volta trova spazio nelle ipotesi ufficiali della Lega Serie A.

L'Inter gioca a calcio, quella di Chivu come quella di Inzaghi. Poi si disconnette. Chivu ha voluto Jones, Inzaghi ha voluto Arnautovic: tutti sbagliano. Ma perché non si discute mai di chi va in campo?

L'Inter deve guardarsi dentro e trovare delle soluzioni. Detto che la difesa è meno consistente, io rimetterei Bisseck titolare. Mauricio Pochettino has vowed to reset the culture at Manchester United as he lifted the lid on being in the stands in 1999 to see the club's greatest triumph.

Pochettino was officially appointed as United's latest head coach on Wednesday and took charge of training for the first time on Thursday.

The Argentine was pictured greeting his latest squad, with several stars having returned from international duty, before attentions turned to preparing the Red Devils for Sunday's trip to Anfield.

Pochettino also addressed the club's internal media team for the first time, outlining how he plans to drag this underperforming squad up the table.

'The culture is the most important,' Pochettino explained.

'Create the habits, the principles, and I think that is what we want to create.

Mauricio Pochettino took Man United first team training for the first time on Thursday.

Matheus Cunha and Lisandro Martinez were among those to report back after international duty.

Man United will hope to hit the ground running under Pochettino when they face Liverpool on Sunday.

'We need to [be] looking forward and to find a way to create the best habits and the culture that makes us to be close to winning every single game.'.

'The players need to express their talent. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most important thing and that is our priority now – it's to work with them and try to take the pressure.'.

Pochettino's determination to be the man to bring winning football back to Old Trafford is in large part due to one of his founding memories of the club back in 1999 when he was a player at Espanyol.

Alongside his now trusted goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez, Pochettino was at the Nou Camp to see United clinch the Champions League, thus sealing a famous Treble, against Bayern Munich.

Recent findings suggest that 'In 1999, I was in Barcelona for that final. That was an iconic final,' he added.

'Toni Jimenez [was there] too. We were shouting for Manchester United from there. I was so excited to see Manchester United.

'This [is the] type of game that you stay sitting in your place [for] and you're so excited because you are watching the game. That was an amazing game.

It has been revealed that 'And then what happened in the end... it's like it's impossible not to empathise with that team, no?

'That was an amazing memory that made me pay more attention to United, to [Sir Alex] Ferguson and the players that were there, that are all legends.'.

That level of success feels a lifetime away from the current squad, which emerges from the international break for a trip to face bitter rivals Liverpool at Anfield slumped 18th in the Premier League.

Pochettino wants to focus on the potential of his Man United squad, rather than their current Premier League plight.

Pochettino is determined to shift the culture at Manchester United back to winning.

The Argentine head coach was in the stands in Barcelona cheering for United back in 1999.

While there are those who may be daunted trying to turn around the ship which sunk so far it cost Michael Carrick his job, Pochettino wants to focus on potential, rather than the present.

'It's a mistake to see the [current] situation. We need to see the potential of this club,' a defiant Pochettino added.

Sources indicate that 'Of course, the circumstances are the circumstances, and we need to be responsible for the circumstances. But at the same time, we need to understand that it's a game and, to connect with the game, we need to feel free.

'The players need to express their talent. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most notable thing and that is our priority now – it's to work with them and try to take the pressure [off].

Sources indicate that 'Pressure needs to bring energy, responsibility needs to bring energy. Because if not, it's too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back.

'When you connect with the game, you connect through your talent and when you feel freedom, when you feel happy, when you want to play for your team-mates, when you want to play for your family, when you want to play for your club, your fans.

According to recent reports, 'That is what we need to create all together and I think we have an amazing staff - we were talking a lot today. Then [we need to] settle all the principles and the ideas and to create our own philosophy and start from zero.

'I think with the power of this club and the fans supporting us, I think we will get in the place that we deserve to be.'.

Pochettino touched down in Manchester on Wednesday morning after his overnight flight.

Pochettino poses at his unveiling with United director of football Jason Wilcox on Wednesday.

Recent findings suggest that pochettino knows that time is not on his side ahead of an upcoming week that sees United travel to face Liverpool on Sunday, followed by a Champions League trip to face Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday. The week is rounded out by a home match a week on Saturday against Brentford.

The Argentine head coach touched down in Manchester on Wednesday morning, taking a private jet straight after the final whistle of United States versus Haiti in Cincinnati.

From there he immediately headed to their Carrington training base where he took a tour and met players and staff, including Tom Heaton, Luke Shaw, Mason Mount and Bruno Fernandes. It is understood he left a good first impression on the players.

And yet, in spite of such a packed schedule, which saw him leave Carrington very late at night on Wednesday and reappear bright and early on Thursday for training, Pochettino is raring to go and is eager for his players to head to Anfield on Sunday convinced they can win.

'I have plenty of energy. It's a privilege to be head coach of Manchester United,' he remarked.

It has been revealed that 'And we are not wasting time. We need to be ready to compete on Sunday.

According to recent reports, 'Now it's not time to think about rest, it's not time to think about sleep. It's about being ready and to prepare everything to be sure that we are going to compete in the best condition at Anfield.'.

Tottenham Hotspur have never before in the club’s history begun a league season without scoring a single goal in the first four games, although having done so after spending £329m on new players really does take some doing.

Spurs have tried to outrun their past but it just keeps catching up with them.

I am sorry for the result that it’s not immediately the improvement. We played as a team. We didn’t score. We didn’t win [but] we played as a team.”.

He joked that in Italy he would be lauded for two consecutive clean sheets in this game and the previous one against Nottingham Forest. “What did you write?” he demanded of one of the Italian newspaper correspondents. “You have the passport.”.

Sources indicate that spurs have one last game at home this month, on Saturday against Aston Villa, to end the streak in September. Recent findings suggest that at the end De Zerbi could not contain his frustration, unable to wait until he reached the privacy of the dressing room to tell Mathys Tel where he had gone wrong. De Zerbi said later that he was simply reminding his player of what it took to play as a central striker.

In a recent development, “There is a term in Italian, ‘sbloccare’ that literally translates as ‘unblock’… I know we can score goals and win games. We have to respect the history of the players – if you forget [Dominic] Solanke and [Omar] Marmoush the others haven’t scored many in their careers. I think we can find the goals with the quality of the players.”.

Antonio Nocerino, allenatore del Napoli Primavera, ha parlato dopo la sconfitta contro il Manchester City per 4-1 in Youth League:.

“Siamo partiti male. Sembra che quando giochiamo queste partite si pensi di più a quello che c’è intorno, al rispetto per l’altra squadra, e non si pensi più a ciò che si deve fare in campo. Ai ragazzi per il secondo tempo ho detto di mettere ciò che avevano, di giocare, perché non avevano nulla da perdere, con coraggio e intensità. Abbiamo avuto delle opportunità, abbiamo preso una traversa, poi ci sono state delle situazioni a nostro favore che potevano essere finalizzate in maniera diversa. Mi porto a casa la reazione, l’approccio della ripresa, ovviamente sapendo anche contro chi abbiamo giocato. Va dato anche merito all’avversario, sono forti.

It has been revealed that club Brugge? Noi in tutte le partite vogliamo provare a fare risultato, anche lì, se dobbiamo chiudere, dobbiamo farlo nel migliore dei modi. Dev’esserci sempre quella speranza che non deve mai mancare. Dobbiamo giocarcela come sempre, l’obiettivo è fare bene e portare soprattutto in casa a vincere. È un sogno però ci vogliamo provare fino alla fine.

Campionato e Coppa Italia? Dobbiamo lavorare bene e recuperare le forze, oltre a mettere una mentalità un po’ diversa. Dobbiamo cercare di essere più aggressivi, vogliosi, più forti nell’uno contro uno e finalizzare un po’ di più quello che creiamo. Costruiamo tanto, arriviamo negli ultimi metri, ma abbiamo poca cattiveria nel chiudere l’azione. È una situazione secondo me individuale e mentale di ogni singolo giocatore. Noi alleniamo tanto i tiri e le situazioni di gioco, però poi c’è anche l’individualità del giocatore. Quando noi ti mettiamo in una condizione di tirare o di fare l’azione da gol, bisogna avere la cattiveria, la fame di fare gol. A noi manca un po’ questo. Finora siamo stati un po’ troppo ‘belli’, e in alcune situazioni dobbiamo essere un po’ più sporchi”.

Secondo quanto appreso da Milannews.it, il Milan, in vista della sfida di Europa League di giovedì in casa dell'Olympiacos, ha messo a disposizione  dei propri tifosi che saranno ad Atene 15 pullman per raggiungere lo stadio Georgios Karaiskakis.

Queste le info su come raggiungere l'impianto:.

•    Sarà predisposto un servizio navette riservato SOLO ai tifosi con biglietto del SETTORE OSPITI. •    Il punto di partenza del servizio navette sarà il MEETING POINT (Kallimarmaro Panathenaic Stadium), aperto dalle 13:30 del giorno partita. •    Le navette partiranno in direzione stadio a partire dal primo pomeriggio; il servizio proseguirà poi al termine della partita riportando i tifosi all’aeroporto al meeting point. •    Per tutti coloro che dovessero arrivare in ritardo o per qualsivoglia motivo non usufruire del servizio navette, le autorità locali e il Club SCONSIGLIANO caldamente l’utilizzo di MEZZI PUBBLICI e invitano a UTILIZZARE SOLO I TAXI per raggiungere lo stadio. •    Coloro che si muoveranno con mezzi propri dovranno comunque raggiungere il meeting point da dove partirà la scorta per parcheggiarsi all’interno del P3 (Parcheggio Settore Ospiti).

Va bene il suo inno “pazza Inter amala”, ma ora sta esagerando, passa da uno stato di schizofrenia calcistica all’altro. Comincia il campionato e si specializza nelle rimonte, sotto di due gol col Napoli e ne fa tre, sotto di due con l’Udinese e rimonta con cinque, ancora sotto con la Roma, col Bologna, con la Fiorentina e ribalta o pareggia. Poi arriva il derby e non rimonta più. Allora cambia registro, trova il Como, segna due gol e non lo fa mai giocare. Problema tecnico-tattico-mentale risolto? Si poteva pensare di sì fino al minuto 35 di Atalanta-Inter, quando i campioni d’Italia erano già in viaggio verso la Pinetina con due gol di vantaggio. Ha segnato Elmas ed è cominciata la baraonda.

Tre volte avanti di due reti, toccava agli altri recuperare. E hanno recuperato. Perché l’Inter è una squadra troppo irregolare, non ha un punto di equilibrio, può fare tutto e il contrario di tutto, ma se vuole difendere lo scudetto non deve mai e poi mai buttare via quelle vittorie, soprattutto non deve e non può prendere tutti questi gol. Negli ultimi 10 campionati, solo una volta (stagione 2021-22) alla 12ª giornata la squadra (il Milan) che vincerà lo scudetto aveva subìto più gol di quanti ne ha presi oggi l’Inter: 19 a 17. Ai tempi in cui vinceva la Juve difficilmente a questo punto del campionato era in doppia cifra nella casella delle reti subite. E la squadra, poi campione, che in questo decennio ha incassato meno gol è stata proprio l’Inter di Simone Inzaghi nel 23-24, appena 6, quell’anno vinse lo scudetto con una difesa super: 22 reti subite alla 38ª, soltanto 5 in più di quante ne ha oggi sulla schiena alla 12ª.

It has been revealed that È una squadra un po’ in là con gli anni e il sistema difensivo non è più efficace come una volta. Quando nel secondo tempo l’Atalanta ha alzato il livello atletico della partita, l’Inter è andata in difficoltà. Può darsi pure che i continui cambiamenti di Chivu nel terzetto difensivo non aiutino a trovare compattezza, ma anche l’anno scorso (chiuso con lo scudetto) l’allenatore cambiava di continuo, già nelle prime cinque giornate aveva modificato ogni volta la difesa. Che ha interpreti di livello internazionale, Bastoni è titolare in Nazionale, Akanji è capitano della Svizzera, Bisseck è stato richiamato da Klopp nella Germania, Pavard è campione del mondo con la Francia nel 2018, Carlos Augusto (un po’ difensore, un po’ esterno) è stato finora uno dei nerazzurri più in forma. E il portiere? Ecco, il portiere sembra l’esemplificazione della sua squadra: Martinez è capace di tutto, nel bene e nel male. In più è una difesa poco protetta.

It has been revealed that A centrocampo l’Inter ha un regista classico, Calhanoglu, un altro... dinamico, Barella, più una mezz’ala vera, Mkhitaryan o Sucic o Zielinski. Non ha un mediano di quelli tosti, non a caso ha cercato Koné, l’ideale per rendere più robusta la fase difensiva. A Bergamo gli errori individuali si sono accumulati a quelli collettivi creando un disastro difensivo. Sul primo gol, Elmas taglia fra Mkhitaryan e Dimarco che in area gli lasciano una libertà assurda. Il secondo è preceduto da un angolo con palla sul primo palo dove si trovano tre atalantini e nessun interista, Martinez mette ancora in angolo e sulla seconda battuta Esposito sbaglia il tempo dello staccom così De Ketelaere segna. Il terzo sempre di CDK è il capitolo più interessante del manuale “come non si marca in area di rigore”: otto interisti, più ovviamente Martinez, e cinque atalantini, di quegli otto almeno cinque sono staccati di metri da chi devono marcare. Il quarto è individuale ed è tutto di Bastoni: non si salta più con le braccia alte, perché sennò è rigore. Lo dovrebbe sapere".

Il turco è molto più di un semplice regista. Sa dettare i tempi, verticalizzare, accompagnare l’azione e garantire quantità. L’Inter, del resto, deve anche pensare al futuro e inserire giovani di qualità, capaci di crescere accanto a un centrocampista che conosce perfettamente il peso della maglia nerazzurra.

Il dilemma, dunque, non è soltanto se rinnovare o meno, ma come farlo. Perché il calcio cambia, le esigenze di una squadra evolvono e anche un campione deve trovare una nuova dimensione, ma il talento, la visione di gioco e la leadership non si misurano con la carta d’identità. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:00 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 04:24 EST, 20 November 2026.

It has been revealed that the man parked up in a nondescript green Ford Fiesta cut an incongruous sight in the affluent residential neighbourhood of Casal Palocco, in south-west Rome, but no one paid him much notice. He made no eye contact and at no stage stepped from the car.

It was only after the street’s famous resident, AS Roma’s Belgian midfielder Radja Nainggolan, had his home burgled and an extraordinary £400,000 worth of possessions stolen that the player’s then wife, Claudia, six months pregnant at that time in April 2016, recalled the Eastern European-looking man in the battered vehicle up their street.

He was Vlada Djuric, a 50-year-old Macedonian of Romani descent and part of the wider Nikolov family, including his wife Zora Jovanovic, their two sons and daughter, whose highly organised thefts from the homes of top footballers would continue for more than a decade, with imprisonment deemed only a minor setback.

While the Nainggolans were blithely unaware of the criminal family’s lookout man – they’d gone to visit friends nearby for a couple of hours and hadn't even bothered to activate the burglar alarm – the assailants were primed to seize the chance.

The two sons, Valentino and Giacomo, mounted the villa’s perimeter wall, opening one door with a magnetic card and jimmying another with a screwdriver, and proceeded undisturbed through the house in 27 minutes, throwing the proceeds of their burglary into a bag as they went.

There were 15 watches (Rolex, Patek Philippe and others) valued at £250,000 and 20 pieces of jewellery, including a diamond worth £25,000. Security cameras on a landing and in an internal room filmed them but such was their confidence, they only partially covered their faces.

Former Roma midfielder Radja Nainggolan and his then wife Claudia, who was six months pregnant, were the targets of a burglary in 2016 (Source: Instagram/Claudia_lai_82).

Nainggolan had an extraordinary £400,000 worth of possessions taken, including 15 watches.

It was old-fashioned detective work from a local officer, Bruno Failla, which led police to a rambling home at Lurano, a small town six hours drive away in Lombardy, at which the Nikolovs would lavishly entertain other members of the Romani community.

The watches matched the descriptions of those stolen from the Nainggolans, though it was a necklace with a Roma logo, and the pair of red shoes with Nainggolan's initials, which really gave the game away.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I ask again for vigilance and watchfulness, please,’ Failla said at the time, because this was the fourth time that footballers' properties in Casal Palocco had been targeted in the space of five years. But the challenge of placing footballers in a state of constant vigilance became clear fully seven years on, when another Nainggolan residence, in Antwerp, Belgium, was burgled while his relatives held a party there.

‘It is one of the most complicated and consistently challenging parts of our security work,’ one former special forces soldier now providing security for footballers tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘It’s been a major sector of our work for years now, but the movements of these clients are so public and that’s irresistible to criminals. The wealth is very evident.’.

One of the sons, Valentino, was jailed for two years in 2016 and other members of his family also did time, but once out, they all set their sights on the Premier League. In 2024, they arrived in the UK via a ferry to Dover from Calais, stopped off in London and made their way north, sleeping in a Ford motorhome and travelling to target homes in a Citroen C3.

A spree of attacks ensued from them on the homes of Alexander Isak, then a Newcastle player, Wolves’ Matheus Cunha (who has subsequently been burgled again while at Manchester United), Birmingham City’s Neil Etheridge and Leon Bailey, with Aston Villa at the time.

A number of Premier League clubs, including Liverpool, Everton and United, are known to have appointed their own security teams to provide an around-the-clock presence at the homes of players who are in squads playing away from home – rather than have that in the hands of a range of private operators.

Some of the top football TV analysts are known to have sought the same security cover outside their houses when away at games.

A number of Premier League clubs, including Liverpool, have appointed their own security teams to provide an around-the-clock presence at the homes of stars who are playing away.

Three masked criminals managed to slip over Bruno Fernandes' security fence and into his home in Nether Alderley, Cheshire, last month and made off with jewellery.

Paul Hughes, managing director of Benchmark Security Group, a leading Manchester-based protection firm, employs former police and Royal security drivers to train his clients in the art of 'defensive driving'.

In a two-hour session, they learn how to avoid being 'boxed in' – as Ozil and Kolasinac were – when approaching traffic lights. Techniques include never taking up a position in the middle lane, avoiding the outside lane if there is a central barrier, and always maintaining sight of the tyres of the vehicle in front when you slow.

'If you can see the tyres, you will always have room to manoeuvre right or left of the car in front, at speed, without hitting it,' Hughes claims.

His staff are often asked to escort clients in their fleet of vehicles, which includes two Land Rovers with blacked-out windows. The firm acquired a Darkfighter Dome – a night-vision camera which is mounted on to the roof of its security vehicles – allowing them to see would-be assailants in the dark. Escorted school runs are also part of the protection they offer.

A screen which dominates Benchmark's underground headquarters, at anonymous premises in Manchester, revealed the fortresses that players' houses have become, when I visited.

It highlighted live feeds from the gardens of mansions which are criss-crossed by infra-red beams. An alarm is triggered in the control room if anyone not approved through face-recognition software is picked up by up to 18 pan, tilt and zoom cameras at a property.

Loudspeakers, operated from the control room, warn off intruders. A team of security staff is never more than six minutes away. A patrol is on the scene of an alert, usually within 90 seconds.

It has been revealed that A number of Manchester United players have invested in specialised security dogs from the Leicester-based firm Chaperone K9 at a cost of up to £20,000 each, though some sources suggest demand has receded as many players have young children. Security firms have their own dogs.

Recent findings suggest that benchmark are one of Britain's most trusted operators – industry-accredited, with former senior police officers on their staff. But this is also a world in which some unsavoury individuals are looking to extract gain.

Daily Mail Sport is aware that a number of current players have paid protection money to ensure they remain safe and are not venturing out socially without having done so. The ‘panic rooms’ some install in their homes, with security card access, are a place to hide valuables.

In a recent development, la Juventus è al lavoro per il mercato di gennaio ma non mancano problemi, limitazioni, questioni ancora da risolvere. Luciano Spalletti grida e chiede un centravanti ma l'operato di Giovanni Carnevali, Frederic Massara e di Marco Ottolini è già ben chiaro da tempo. E sanno benissimo dove andare ad agire, ma devono anche tener conto di diversi parametri e problemi ancora da risolvere. Un centravanti non può cadere dal cielo, perché ci sono problemi di lista, di conti e di rosa da considerare.

La Juventus vuole un 9 ma per questioni di lista in caso di arrivo di un giocatore straniero, deve cederne uno straniero. La Juventus ha ancora a disposizione 1 slot per tesserare un calciatore extracomunitario proveniente dall'estero in questa stagione, ma non può inserirlo nella lista Serie A senza prima liberare un posto nella lista dei 17 "Over 22" non formati in Italia. Diverso il discorso sarebbe in caso di arrivo di un giocatore italiano, in quel caso potrebbe far partire (eccezioni a parte sugli italiani, chiaramente, per quelli formatisi all'estero) anche un italiano.

Non solo: Anche se il club può formalmente tesserare un nuovo extracomunitario, il regolamento della Serie A impone un limite massimo di 25 giocatori in rosa, di cui solo 17 liberi da vincoli di formazione. La Juventus ha tutti e 17 questi slot già pieni, al punto da aver dovuto escludere calciatori come Arkadiusz Milik e Khephren Thuram, e potrà effettuare al massimo 2 sostituzioni di giocatori di movimento nel corso dell'intera stagione. E il francese verrà reintegrato in rosa, per questo uno dovrà uscire. Chi? L'indiziato numero uno è Teun Koopmeiners, che a gennaio peserà a bilancio per 25,8 milioni di euro e ne guadagna 5,77 lordi a stagione. Come già detto e ribadito in passato: al momento dell'acquisto, c'era la fila delle squadre in Italia e in Europa per prenderlo, poi l'olandese non è riuscito ad adattarsi (ma l'impressione che possa tornare grande altrove...). Cederlo a queste cifre sarà dura, ma per rimetter dentro Thuram, e verrà fatto, uno dovrà essere tolto dalla lista.

It has been revealed that A questo si lega dunque la questione del terzino. Vuoi un 'Alejandro Baldé'? Deve partire Juan Cabal. Altrimenti un italiano per Andrea Cambiaso, semplice. E lo stesso in attacco. Certo, dovesse arrivare Gianluca Scamacca dall'Atalanta, lì davanti potrebbe partire Edon Zhegrova (indiziato ma anche lì, mica facile), e allora andrebbe bene anche cedere Cambiaso per prendere un terzino. Insomma, l'intreccio è chiaro (ma complicato) e in questo la Juventus deve anche rientrare nei paletti del settlement agreement. Tanti fattori, adesso sta camminando su un sottile filo e gli investimenti a gennaio sembrano da escludere a meno di una maxi cessione.

Inside Newcastle United's transfer tension: Matthias Jaissle wants greater control as he eyes a new No 10 and No 9 in January - but the next four fixtures could make or break him and the club's season, writes CRAIG HOPE

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (978 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:49 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 05:54 EST, 20 November 2026.
  • This time, Matthias Jaissle wants his fingerprints on the bank notes.
  • Recent findings suggest that the need for reinforcement is clear, even on the back of £270million invested in the summer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:49 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 05:54 EST, 20 November 2026.

This time, Matthias Jaissle wants his fingerprints on the bank notes. But what the head coach wishes for in January, and what Newcastle United are willing and able to give, is likely to be very different. When that happens, it rarely ends well - on the pitch or off it.

Recent findings suggest that the need for reinforcement is clear, even on the back of £270million invested in the summer. Jaissle knows as much and is not afraid to say so. The rookie German has to protect himself as much as he does his club.

Recent findings suggest that because, as Newcastle prepare for what threatens to be a long and testing winter, Jaissle is revisiting the brochure presented to him in the summer. And that is the 38-year-old's concern and frustration - the prospectus for the season ahead was not of his making.

Recent findings suggest that he arrived three weeks before the start of the campaign and with four of eight signings already through the door. At a cost of £110m, that quartet have started just three Premier League games between them, and each of those by teenager Sean Steur. Baz Toure and Aladji Bamba are virtual spectators, while reserve keeper Ewen Jaouen is injured.

In a recent development, for Jaissle, you suspect, that money was not spent as he would have advised, had he been in situ. Now, in the new year, he wants greater control, as well as a No 10 and No 9. For any Newcastle follower averse to tension, you best watch this transfer window through your fingertips.

Jaissle, sporting director Ross Wilson and chief executive David Hopkinson are the protagonists who will navigate January. At least, that is, if Jaissle makes it into 2027. He deserves that time - not least because of the turbulent and transitional situation he inherited - but the next four fixtures will potentially make or break him and the season.

Head coach Matthias Jaissle is seeking greater control of Newcastle United's transfer strategy.

Aladji Bamba has been a virtual spectator and joined in the summer before Jaissle's arrival.

After the visit of league leaders Arsenal on Saturday, there is a trip to second-placed Brighton, followed by a seismic home double header in the space of five days against Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United and bitter rivals Sunderland.

It is why, despite rumblings behind the scenes in recent days of potential transfer discord, Jaissle was on message - the collective, club message - when I asked him about the profile of player he might want in January.

Sources indicate that 'It's not the time to talk about the transfer window,' he noted. 'We have players capable to deliver higher performances on the pitch. We have big quality, not only up front, but throughout the whole squad. We believe we can do better and this is what we now want to influence.'.

Industry observers note that however, there was a softening when I sympathised with the head coach over him being judged by a window for which he did not have ownership. Did he, then, want more influence this time?

'Now, it's a different story (compared to the summer), if you're already in and also if you have clarified your clear idea, your clear needs, it's going to be easier,' he said.

In a recent development, 'But the transfer market is still a long time ahead, at least it feels like that right now with our fixtures. Our task, especially from my stance, is to focus on the next match and the upcoming challenges.'.

Jaissle knows that his case will only be strengthened by a steadying of results, even though, conversely, more defeats would heighten the need for signings. They have lost four from six in all competitions.

According to recent reports, the problem is that the hierarchy are on the record as stating the summer business went pretty much exactly as they wished and believed they had a squad for the entire season. There are also Squad Cost Ratio limitations. It is understood there is headroom for one player, but not the two the manager would prefer and not at a fee approaching the £51m they paid for Matias Fernandez-Pardo on deadline day.

Jaissle wants a fresh No 9 to compete with the likes of Yoane Wisse who has one league goal.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo (left) has failed to impress so far at Newcastle after his £51m arrival.

According to recent reports, the 21-year-old forward is another problem. He is still to score from seven appearances and there is a fear he is not yet strong enough for the Premier League. Interestingly, Jaissle revealed on Thursday his dismay that he was booked during the 1-1 draw at Fulham last time out for screaming at Fernandez-Pardo to stand up.

Industry observers note that that is not to say Jaissle does not believe in the talent of those brought in. He does. But for a coach in his first season in a major European league, he needs players who can impact today, not tomorrow. He needs, and wants, more experience. One of his first recommendations in August was to sign 31-year-old midfielder Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg. Nico Gonzalez eventually arrived in that position, but the 24-year-old looks like a player who has spent two seasons in reserve at Manchester City.

So, it is easy to see why Jaissle needs and wants more in January. It is also easy to see why he might not get it. There could be trouble ahead, and that is not just the upcoming matches.

In the thick Naples air in midweek, Declan Rice did what he always does: he kept running. Another start for the Arsenal midfielder, another 90 minutes completed and another performance of constructive passing and destructive defending. For anyone who was worried about Rice’s physical condition, it was an emphatic response.

After that Champions League victory over Napoli, Rice insisted he was ready for another marathon campaign. He made 69 appearances for club and country last season, up from 60 the previous term, and believes that is a sustainable number of games, even for an all-action midfielder such as himself. “I have shown I can do it,” he said.

The key question, though, is not whether Rice can do it, but whether he should do it. There is no doubt that his body eventually began to pay the price for his exertions last year, especially during the World Cup, and it would be reasonable for his managers to worry that his extraordinary workload might one day take a serious toll. This, after all, is a footballer who managed nerve pain in his hamstring throughout the second half of last season.

Sunderland are the latest team tasked with stopping Arsenal, who have begun their title defence in formidable style: they’ve won out of three, including a dominant comeback victory against Chelsea last weekend, and look well equipped to become the first Arsenal team to retain the title since the mid-1930s.

Recent findings suggest that “I love those challenges,” stated Mikel Arteta. “I try to create them in pre-seasons so when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So get to the stadium very late, change the routine and suddenly the players have to do something else.

Industry observers note that arteta has tested his squad in a variety of ways. “[We have] delayed the meals, delayed the transport, taken a different route. 42′ Cross pericolosi di Lang e Politano, manca solo all’ultimo colpo.

38′ Chance per McTominay che di testa impatta debolmente.

34′ Cross pericoloso City, chiude Beukema.

32′ Chance Napoli con Politano che sbaglia l’ultimo passaggio.

27′ Hojlund ci prova da posizione defilata, blocca Donnarumma.

24′ Cross insidioso di Enzo Fernandez, Milinkovic respinge a fatica smanacciando.

18′ Chance per Allan che viene murato dalla difesa.

15′ Buona partenza del Napoli che sembra reggere l’impatto inglese.

9′ Ci prova O’Reilly che si inserisce, palla a lato.

7′ Tiro di McTominay, palla deviata di poco a lato.

6′ Chance per McTominay, la difesa chiude in extremis.

1′ Subito Anderson dal limite, ci prova e respinge Milinkovic.

MANCHESTER CITY (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma; Nunes, Gvardiol, Guehi, O’Reilly; Bouaddi, Anderson; Allan, Enzo Fernandez, Cherki; Haaland. Allenatore: Maresca. A disposizione: Rulli, Ruben Dias, Ndiaye, Kovacic, Doku, Ait-Nouri, Vitor Reis, Khusanov, Foden, McAidoo, Samba, Lewis.

According to recent reports, NAPOLI (3-5-1-1): Milinkovic-Savic; Beukema, Rrahmani, Olivera; Politano, De Bruyne, Gilmour, McTominay, Spinazzola; Lang; Hojlund. Allenatore: Massimiliano Allegri. A disposizione: Contini, Spinelli, Chiummariello, Neres, Lucca, Giovane, Anguissa.
